paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. This one is heavy, so I'll say it plain. In this passage, God's word brings down a mighty nation, and it's not a small thing. Egypt looked great, and the message asks her, "Whom do you surpass in beauty?" (Ezekiel 32:19). Then it sends her down with the others (Ezekiel 32:18-19).

Look at who's already down there: Assyria, Elam, Meshech and Tubal, Edom, the leaders of the north and the Sidonians. They all spread terror in the land of the living, and the passage says it again and again (Ezekiel 32:23-26, 30). Every one of them thought their might would keep them standing. But it didn't, and Edom's kings and princes are laid among those slain by the sword "despite their might" (Ezekiel 32:29). So here's what I'm taking from it: power doesn't last, and no army is bigger than the Lord GOD.

So why does it matter to you? God has the last word, and He says, "For I will spread My terror in the land of the living" (Ezekiel 32:32). Nothing people build up can stand against that, and I can't either, so I'm glad to be on His side. Keep your ovens warm, friend, and keep your trust in Him instead of in anything that looks big and shiny.
